advances: The three-layer lift has an exact reflection ledger at every integer center, including all within-middle-layer pairs created by new lattice sites. Its reflection bound is equivalent to explicit conditions on the complete middle layer, not merely on selected cross-layer midpoint centers. Independently of these local conditions, its lattice hull has at least \(v_D+n+1\) vertices. Consequently the proposed vertex recurrence \(v_{D'}=v_D+2\) is impossible for \(n\ge2\). For the accepted twenty-point tetrahedron, every integer apex fails to preserve maximum reflection count three, so neither a finite apex search nor the proposed cardinality recurrence can repair this particular lift mechanism.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The slice calculation, reflection ledger, vertex containment, and obstruction are proved here by elementary convexity and finite counting. Accepted fact 768d9712b73c4ab7 is used only for its stated vertex-deficit inequality and its exact twenty-point tetrahedron data.
proof:
First compute the real slices. Every point of \(P'\) is a convex combination of the bottom layer, the layer at height one, and the apex. By convexity of \(P\), it has a representation

\[
\alpha(p,0)+\beta(q,1)+\gamma(a,2),
\qquad p,q\in P,\quad
\alpha,\beta,\gamma\ge0,\quad
\alpha+\beta+\gamma=1.
\]

If its height is zero, then \(\beta=\gamma=0\), so its horizontal coordinate belongs to \(P\). If its height is two, then \(\alpha=\beta=0\), so it is the apex. At height one, \(\beta+2\gamma=1\) and \(\alpha=\gamma\), and its horizontal coordinate is

\[
(1-2\gamma)q+2\gamma\,(p+a)/2,
\qquad 0\le\gamma\le1/2.
\]

This gives precisely \(\operatorname{conv}(P\cup(P+a)/2)\): conversely, a combination with weight \(\lambda\) on \((p+a)/2\) is realized by weights \(\lambda/2\) on the bottom point and apex and weight \(1-\lambda\) on the height-one point. All heights lie in \([0,2]\). Taking integer points proves the census, including \(D\subseteq D_1\). For \(p\in D\) with \(p\equiv a\pmod2\), the point \((p+a)/2\) is an integer point of this middle slice, proving \(\mathcal C_a\subseteq D_1\).

For a center \((x,0)\), reflected endpoints must have nonnegative heights adding to zero. Both endpoints therefore lie on the bottom layer, giving exactly \(r_D(x)\) oriented displacements. Similarly, at height two both endpoints must lie at height two, giving one displacement at \(x=a\) and none elsewhere. At height one, the endpoint heights can only be \(1,1\), \(0,2\), or \(2,0\). The first case contributes \(r_{D_1}(x)\). The other two cases use the apex and the unique possible bottom endpoint \(2x-a\), and occur if and only if \(2x-a\in D\). Their displacements are distinct and nonzero because their last coordinates are opposite nonzero integers. They therefore contribute exactly two. Heights outside \([0,2]\) cannot support reflected endpoints. This proves the all-center ledger.

For completeness, any integer midpoint of two points of \(D'\) belongs to the convex set \(P'\), hence to \(P'\cap\mathbb Z^{n+1}=D'\). Thus an outside integer center has no reflected pair. The same argument applies to \(D\) and \(D_1\) in their respective convex sets. At any supported center, the zero displacement occurs and all nonzero displacements occur in opposite pairs. Its reflection count is therefore a positive odd integer. The bottom counts already satisfy the hypothesis, and the apex count is one. At a cross-layer center the middle contribution must consequently equal one, whereas at another middle center it must be at most three. These are exactly the stated middle-layer conditions.

At an old center \(x\in D\), all pairs with both endpoints in \(D\), including the zero displacement, contribute precisely \(r_D(x)\). Every additional reflected pair has distinct endpoints and at least one endpoint in \(E\), so it contributes exactly two and is counted once by \(q_E(x)\). This proves the displayed increment formula. Since \(r_D(x)\in\{1,3\}\), it gives the stated conditions at old centers. At a new center the zero displacement contributes one, and every unordered distinct pair contributes two, giving the stated conditions there as well. Their necessity and sufficiency follow by partitioning \(D_1\) into \(D\) and \(E\).

The new-site contribution can fail even where no cross-layer pair occurs. For an exact example, take \(n=1\), \(P=[0,3]\), \(D=\{0,1,2,3\}\), and \(a=-2\). The two endpoint centers of \(D\) have count one, the other two have count three, and outside centers have count zero. The complete middle layer is \(D_1=\{-1,0,1,2,3\}\). At the old center \(x=1\), the original pair \(\{0,2\}\) and the new pair \(\{-1,3\}\), together with the zero displacement, give \(r_{D_1}(1)=5\). There is no cross-layer pair there because \(2x-a=4\notin D\). Thus \(r_{D'}((1,1))=5\) solely from within-middle-layer pairs. This illustrates why auditing only cross-layer midpoint centers is insufficient.

Now put \(K=\operatorname{conv}(D')\). It is a full-dimensional polytope in \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\), since its bottom layer contains the full-dimensional set \(D\) and it contains the apex at height two. Its bottom face is exactly \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\times\{0\}\). The vertices of this face are vertices of \(K\), and no other bottom point is a vertex. The apex is a vertex, being the unique point of \(K\) at height two. Every vertex of a convex hull of a finite set belongs to that set. Therefore all remaining vertices are exactly the points \((x,1)\) with \(x\in T_a\), and

\[
v_{D'}=v_D+1+|T_a|.
\]

It remains to prove \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\subseteq\operatorname{conv}(T_a\cup\{a\})\). Fix any \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and write \(b=\max_{p\in D}c\cdot p\) and \(\mu=\max_{p\in D_1}c\cdot p\). Since \(D\subseteq D_1\), \(\mu\ge b\). If \(b>c\cdot a\), choose \(0<\tau<\mu-c\cdot a\). The linear functional \((x,t)\mapsto c\cdot x+\tau t\) has maximum \(b\) on the bottom layer, maximum \(\mu+\tau>b\) on the middle layer, and value \(c\cdot a+2\tau<\mu+\tau\) at the apex. Its maximizing face on \(K\) consequently consists of middle-layer points. This face contains a vertex of \(K\), whose horizontal coordinate belongs to \(T_a\) and attains \(\mu\). Hence in this case \(\max_{x\in T_a}c\cdot x=\mu\ge b\).

There exists a direction of this case: choose \(p\in D\setminus\{a\}\), which is possible by full-dimensionality, and set \(c=p-a\). Then \(b\ge c\cdot p>c\cdot a\). Thus \(T_a\) is nonempty. For every direction with \(b\le c\cdot a\), the point \(a\) itself has functional value at least \(b\). Combining both cases, the maximum of \(c\cdot x\) on \(\operatorname{conv}(T_a\cup\{a\})\) is at least its maximum on \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\), for every \(c\). This implies the required containment. Indeed, if a point of \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\) lay outside the other compact convex hull, its nearest point in that hull would give a strictly separating linear functional, contradicting the established inequalities.

Because this hull contains a full-dimensional set in \(\mathbb R^n\) and is generated by \(1+|T_a|\) points, its affine dimension is at most \(\lvert T_a\rvert\) and at least \(n\). Therefore \(|T_a|\ge n\), completing the vertex bound. If \(n\ge2\), it gives \(v_{D'}\ge v_D+n+1>v_D+2\).

Finally, both \(D\) and \(D'\) are finite and lattice-convex in the exact sense required by accepted fact 768d9712b73c4ab7. Indeed, \(D\subseteq\operatorname{conv}(D)\subseteq P\) gives \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\cap\mathbb Z^n=D\); similarly, \(D'\subseteq K\subseteq P'\) gives \(K\cap\mathbb Z^{n+1}=D'\), even when \(P'\) is not a lattice polytope. Under the assumption \(\max r_{D'}\le3\), apply that accepted fact in ambient dimension \(n+1\), without substituting affine rank, to obtain

\[
N'\le3\cdot2^{n+1}-v_{D'}
\le6\cdot2^n-v_D-n-1.
\]

The census and \(D\subseteq D_1\) give \(N'\ge2N+1\). Substitute \(N=3\cdot2^n-v_D-\delta\) in these two bounds. Their compatibility is exactly \(v_D+2\delta\ge n+2\). If instead the specified value \(N'=2N+v_D-2\) is imposed, compatibility with the upper bound is

\[
2N+v_D-2\le6\cdot2^n-v_D-n-1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad n-1\le2\delta.
\]

For comparison, substitution of both proposed values \(N'=2N+v_D-2\) and \(v_{D'}=v_D+2\) into the accepted deficit bound gives

\[
2N+v_D-2\le6\cdot2^n-v_D-2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N+v_D\le3\cdot2^n.
\]

This algebraically consistent inequality does not remedy the independently false vertex count in dimensions at least two.

For a saturated simplicial source, \(v_D=n+1\) and \(\delta=0\), the necessary condition \(v_D+2\delta\ge n+2\) is false. Such a source therefore has no preserving apex. In the accepted three-dimensional tetrahedron, accepted fact 768d9712b73c4ab7 supplies \(D=A\), \(N=20\), \(v_D=4\), and \(\max r_D=3\). Every lift has at least \(2\cdot20+1=41\) lattice points and at least \(4+3+1=8\) vertices. If it had maximum reflection count at most three, the accepted bound in dimension four would instead give \(N'\le48-8=40\), a contradiction. An outside center has count zero, and every supported-center count is odd, so failure of the bound three means the maximum is at least five. This proves the claimed all-apex obstruction and finishes the proof.
statement:
Let \(n\ge1\) be an integer, let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be compact and convex, and suppose that \(D=P\cap\mathbb Z^n\) is full-dimensional and satisfies \(\max_{j\in\mathbb Z^n}r_D(j)\le3\). Here, consistently with accepted fact 768d9712b73c4ab7, for a finite set \(B\subseteq\mathbb Z^m\) and an integer center \(j\),

\[
r_B(j)=\bigl|\{u\in\mathbb Z^m:j+u,j-u\in B\}\bigr|,
\]

with oriented displacements and the zero displacement counted once when \(j\in B\). Let \(a\in\mathbb Z^n\), and define

\[
\begin{aligned}
P'&=\operatorname{conv}\bigl((P\times\{0,1\})\cup\{(a,2)\}\bigr),
& D'&=P'\cap\mathbb Z^{n+1},\\
D_1&=\operatorname{conv}\bigl(P\cup (P+a)/2\bigr)\cap\mathbb Z^n,
& \mathcal C_a&=\{(a+p)/2:p\in D,\ p\equiv a\pmod2\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

The congruence is coordinatewise. Write \(N=|D|\), \(N'=|D'|\), and let \(v_D\) and \(v_{D'}\) count the vertices of \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\) and \(\operatorname{conv}(D')\), respectively. These definitions also cover the usual complete-set representation \(P=\operatorname{conv}(D)\); the conclusions do not require that additional equality.

The complete lattice census and the all-center reflection ledger are

\[
D'=(D\times\{0\})\cup(D_1\times\{1\})\cup\{(a,2)\},
\qquad N'=N+|D_1|+1,
\]

\[
r_{D'}((x,t))=
\begin{cases}
r_D(x),&t=0,\\
r_{D_1}(x)+2\mathbf 1_{\{2x-a\in D\}},&t=1,\\
\mathbf 1_{\{x=a\}},&t=2,\\
0,&t\notin\{0,1,2\},
\end{cases}
\qquad (x,t)\in\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb Z.
\]

In particular \(D\subseteq D_1\), \(\mathcal C_a\subseteq D_1\), and every integer center outside \(D'\) has reflection count zero.

The condition \(\max r_{D'}\le3\) holds if and only if

\[
r_{D_1}(x)=1\quad(x\in\mathcal C_a),
\qquad
r_{D_1}(x)\le3\quad(x\in D_1\setminus\mathcal C_a).
\]

This equivalence includes the contribution of every new middle-layer site. More explicitly, put \(E=D_1\setminus D\). For \(x\in D\), let \(q_E(x)\) be the number of unordered distinct pairs \(\{p,q\}\subseteq D_1\) with \(p+q=2x\) and at least one endpoint in \(E\). Then

\[
r_{D_1}(x)=r_D(x)+2q_E(x)\qquad(x\in D).
\]

Thus an old center in \(\mathcal C_a\) must have \(r_D(x)=1\) and \(q_E(x)=0\). At an old center outside \(\mathcal C_a\), one must have \(q_E(x)=0\) if \(r_D(x)=3\), and \(q_E(x)\le1\) if \(r_D(x)=1\). At a new center \(x\in E\), the number of unordered distinct pairs in \(D_1\) with midpoint \(x\) must be zero when \(x\in\mathcal C_a\), and at most one otherwise. These old-center and new-center requirements together are necessary and sufficient.

Define

\[
T_a=\{x\in D_1:(x,1)\text{ is a vertex of }\operatorname{conv}(D')\}.
\]

Then

\[
\operatorname{conv}(D)\subseteq\operatorname{conv}(T_a\cup\{a\}),
\qquad |T_a|\ge n,
\qquad v_{D'}=v_D+1+|T_a|\ge v_D+n+1.
\]

In particular the proposed vertex recurrence \(v_{D'}=v_D+2\) cannot hold in any dimension \(n\ge2\), regardless of reflection counts.

Accepted fact 768d9712b73c4ab7 gives \(N\le3\cdot2^n-v_D\); set \(\delta=3\cdot2^n-v_D-N\ge0\). If the lift satisfies \(\max r_{D'}\le3\), that fact in ambient dimension \(n+1\), together with the preceding vertex bound, implies

\[
2N+1\le N'\le6\cdot2^n-v_D-n-1,
\qquad v_D+2\delta\ge n+2.
\]

If additionally the proposed cardinality recurrence \(N'=2N+v_D-2\) holds, then necessarily \(n-1\le2\delta\). Substituting both proposed recurrences into the accepted deficit bound alone merely recovers \(N+v_D\le3\cdot2^n\); it does not establish the vertex recurrence or any reflection condition.

In particular, any full-dimensional source with \(v_D=n+1\) and \(N=3\cdot2^n-v_D\) admits no integer apex \(a\) preserving \(\max r_{D'}\le3\) in this construction. The source in accepted fact 768d9712b73c4ab7 is such a source: specialize \(D=A\) and \(P\) to its tetrahedron, so \(n=3\), \(N=20\), \(v_D=4\), and \(\delta=0\). For every \(a\in\mathbb Z^3\), its lift has \(\max r_{D'}\ge5\). Hence this excludes in particular every suggested choice \(a=2v-x\) with \(v\) an old vertex and \(x\in A\), without a finite search. This is an obstruction to this three-layer recurrence, not a claim about the locked mixed-integer depth problem.
